events.content:
**Bottom line:** Google and Amazon do not disclose standalone TPU or Trainium revenue, respectively, so there is no company-reported, auditable market-share figure for either accelerator in 2025 or 2026. Amazon’s disclosed figure combines Trainium with Graviton—more than a $10 billion annual revenue run rate at Q4 2025—rather than separating Trainium. [[1]]

| Market-share measure | 2025 | 2026 estimate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Google TPU | Not disclosed / no robust independent 2025 figure found | ~6–8% of data-center AI-accelerator revenue or deployed-FLOPS-based market, depending on the methodology used. [[2]]|
| AWS Trainium / Inferentia | Not disclosed / no robust independent 2025 figure found | ~2–3% in one 2026 estimate; a separate August 2026 analyst-based estimate puts the combined Trainium/Inferentia share near 5%. [[2]] [[3]]|

The appropriate 2026 takeaway is therefore **TPU roughly 6–8% and Trainium/Inferentia roughly 2–5%**, but these are third-party estimates rather than reported results and should not be treated as precise, directly comparable revenue shares. [[2]] [[3]]

**What supports the direction of share gains:** AWS stated that Trainium2 was fully subscribed, with **1.4 million chips landed** by its Q4 2025 results, and that it powered most Bedrock inference; this demonstrates rapid adoption but does not establish Trainium-only revenue or market share. [[4]] [[1]] Google’s TPU scale was also reinforced by Anthropic’s commitment for access to up to **one million TPUs**, with capacity coming online through 2026, although that is a capacity commitment rather than TPU revenue recognized by Google. [[3]]

**Market context:** ASIC-based AI-server shipments are projected to reach **27.8%** of the server market in 2026, with custom-ASIC shipments forecast to grow **44.6% year over year**, versus **16.1%** for merchant GPUs; that expansion is the structural reason TPU and Trainium can gain share even while Nvidia remains dominant. [[5]] Estimates still place Nvidia at roughly **73–80%** of AI-accelerator revenue in mid-2026, so TPU and Trainium remain meaningful but distinctly secondary platforms in the overall market. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA vs AMD AI accelerator market share 2026

events.content: NVIDIA vs AMD AI accelerator market share 2026

**AI accelerator market share depends materially on the denominator**—GPU-only versus all AI chips, and revenue versus server shipments. [[1]]

| 2024 global AI-server market measure | NVIDIA | AMD | Custom silicon / ASICs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **GPU-equipped AI servers: chip-supplier share** | **Nearly 90%** | **~8%** | Not applicable to the GPU-only denominator |
| **All AI-server chips (GPU, ASIC, FPGA): chip-supplier share** | **~64%** | Not separately disclosed in this measure | The balance is largely ASICs, FPGAs and other suppliers |
| **AI-server mix by system type** | GPUs: **~71%** of AI servers | Included in GPU category | ASIC servers: **~26%** |

TrendForce’s 2024 estimate puts NVIDIA at nearly 90% of the GPU-equipped AI-server market and AMD at roughly 8%; once proprietary ASICs and FPGAs are included, NVIDIA’s share falls to about 64%. [[1]] GPU-based servers represented about 71% of AI servers in 2024, versus approximately 26% for ASIC-based servers, reflecting sizeable deployment of proprietary accelerators by AWS, Meta and other North American cloud providers, as well as Chinese developers. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** NVIDIA retains overwhelming leadership in merchant AI GPUs, while AMD is the principal merchant GPU challenger but remains much smaller. [[1]] Custom silicon—such as Google TPUs and cloud-provider in-house ASICs—is the principal source of NVIDIA share dilution when the market is defined to include all accelerators rather than GPUs alone. [[2]] [[1]]

**Direction of travel:** TrendForce estimated NVIDIA would still hold approximately 70% of the broader AI-chip market in 2025, but expected greater custom-ASIC deployment to reduce that share over time. [[3]] Its 2026 shipment forecast has GPUs still leading at 69.7% of AI-server shipments, while ASIC-based systems rise to 27.8%, their highest share since 2023, with ASIC shipment growth outpacing GPU-system growth. [[4]] 

These figures should not be treated as interchangeable with revenue share: NVIDIA’s premium systems mean that its revenue share can exceed its shipment or unit share. [[5]]

Sources:
[S9.1] Global AI Server Demand Surge Expected to Drive 2024 Market Value to US$187 Billion; Represents 65% of Server Market, Says TrendForce — https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20240717-12227.html
